conflicts: Lifetime of the 27135.695 cm^-1 (9P3) level: the Battles thesis lists 10.98 ns for the "368 nm transition", which is just 1/A of the single 368 nm line (NIST A = 9.1e7 s^-1); the NIST A values of the 368 nm and 371 nm lines together imply an upper-level lifetime of at most 5.5 ns. The thesis number is not entered.

743.014 nm line: the 157Gd isotope shift 486(65) MHz does not follow the sequence of the other isotopes; the authors report a King-plot nonlinearity but also say the 157Gd hyperfine structure was not fully resolved.
Isotope abundances: NIST composition table (entered) vs the slightly different values printed by Chavarría-Sibaja et al. (154Gd 2.15%, 155Gd 14.73%, 157Gd 15.68%, 158Gd 24.87%, 160Gd 21.90%).

Lifetimes 10.8 ns (22334.508) and 13.7 ns (22563.824), now read directly in Den Hartog et al. 2011, are much shorter than 1/A of the single NIST-listed line from each level (26 ns and 33 ns): the old unrated NIST A values (T7227) are too small or other strong branches exist; the Lawler et al. 2011 line table that would settle it is a closed supplement.

Lifetime of 27135.695 (9P3): Den Hartog 2011 gives 3.5 ns (entered) and Xu 2003 3.5(2) ns; Gorshkov 1983 (electron beam) 5.4(5) ns. With the NIST A values of the 368.4 and 371.4 nm lines (9.1e7 + 9.2e7 s-1) lifetime x sum(A) = 0.64. Likewise 27425.245: 4.0 ns vs Xu 3.9(2) and Gorshkov 6.7(5) ns.

Den Hartog 2011 vs other lifetime sets (kept as alternatives): Gorshkov 1983 electron-beam values are longer by 13-65 % (cascade repopulation, per Den Hartog et al.); Xu 2003 agrees below 10 ns but is on average 9 % longer above 10 ns; Wang 2013 agrees within about 5 % (largest difference 31865.242: 5.3 vs 5.7(2) ns).

Ground level 9D°2 hyperfine constants: Unsworth 1969 (entered) A155 = 36.5753(98), B155 = 179.407(44), A157 = 47.9591(76), B157 = 191.161(72) MHz; the LLNL modeling table prints 36.575 / 179.4 / 47.95 / 191.16 MHz without signs - consistent.

notes: Stable isotopes: 155Gd and 157Gd have I = 3/2 (both nuclear moments negative: mu = -0.2591 and -0.3398 nuclear magnetons in the IAEA table); the others have I = 0. Hyperfine convention: E = A K/2 + B [3K(K+1) - 4I(I+1)J(J+1)] / [8I(2I-1)J(2J-1)], K = F(F+1)-J(J+1)-I(I+1) (as printed by Adhikari et al.). Ground-term 9D°J (J = 2-6) hyperfine constants of 155Gd and 157Gd are from Unsworth 1969, Table 1 (scanned PDF pdf/Gd_Unsworth_1969.pdf, numbers checked against the page image, signs as printed); the unsigned LLNL modeling constants for 9D°2 are kept as alternatives and agree in magnitude. The LLNL constants for the 17380.827 level and the 575.19 nm line are modeling inputs printed without signs or uncertainties; treat them as indicative. Lifetimes: all 136 levels of Den Hartog, Bilty, Lawler 2011, Table 1 (pdf/Gd_DenHartog_2011.pdf; parsed from the PDF text, all matched to NIST energy and J within 0.002 cm-1); one common stated uncertainty of ±5 % (unc = 5 % of the value).
